originals.citation: Rafaeli, Sheizaf, and Daphne R. Raban (2003). Experimental Investigation of the Subjective Value of Information in Trading. Journal of the Association for Information Systems 4, 119–139.
originals.first_page_check: Repository cover identifies exact DOI/title/authors; first published page is 119. Repository cover says volume4 issue1 article5; author list/SSRN use4(5). Issue numbering not resolved by silently choosing one.
originals.design_and_sample: 31 honors undergraduates in counterbalanced sell-first/buy-first groups14/17; two warm-ups, six business games, three WTA and three WTP bids each. Two outliers removed, leaving29. Weather information could guide lemonade quality, prices and inventory; rewards related to profits.
originals.published_finding: Reported WTA/WTP approximately3; pooled ratios exceed1, but individual group/repetition WTA–WTP tests were not uniformly significant. Players often bought and rarely sold information despite no demonstrated objective lemonade-profit benefit.
originals.elicitation: Open-ended BDM bids confronted unknown preset market prices. High bids could strategically secure buying/keeping information while payment stayed at market price; authors discuss risk aversion and an unresolved strategic-bidding explanation.

originals.citation: Gillath, Omri, Phillip R. Shaver, Jong-Min Baek, and David S. Chun (2008). Genetic Correlates of Adult Attachment Style. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin 34(10), 1396–1405.
originals.first_page_check: Publisher cover and actual page1396 match title/authors/DOI; article ends1405 with references.
originals.design_and_sample: 147 undergraduates (40men/107women),18–29years. 36-item ECR anxiety/avoidance,18 items each, seven-point response; Big Five covariates and saliva genotyping. OXTR rs53576 G/A: AA47, AG60, GG40. DRD2 A1 and HTR2A T102C also tested.
originals.published_finding: OXTR rs53576 not associated with either attachment dimension. Positive findings concern DRD2 A1A1/anxiety and HTR2A TT/avoidance, not OXTR. The standard ECR concerns close relationship partners; the later current paper explicitly contrasts its friendship version with standard romantic attachment. Gillath’s quoted Methods do not themselves use the word romantic.
access_limits: Different analytic degrees of freedom appear across analyses; no invented uniform endpoint N.
No data-level linkage to Rodrigues or Pearce established.

originals.citation: Rodrigues, Sarina M., Laura R. Saslow, Natalia Garcia, Oliver P. John, and Dacher Keltner (2009). Oxytocin receptor genetic variation relates to empathy and stress reactivity in humans. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 106(50), 21437–21441.
originals.first_page_check: Complete PMC HTML front matter matches title/authors/DOI and printed page interval21437–21441; actual PDF unavailable (PDF endpoint returned HTML). XML route supplies only front matter/abstract because publisher restricts XML; HTML body is complete.
originals.design_and_sample: 192 Berkeley students,59%female,mean20.2years. OXTR rs53576 AA/AG pooled against GG (genotyped AA47/AG88/GG47). RMET behavioral empathy;21-item other-oriented empathy composite; baseline-adjusted heart rate during startle anticipation;12-item affective stress scale. A subset completed shortened ECR explicitly about romantic relationships.
originals.published_finding: GG showed higher behavioral/dispositional empathy and lower physiological/dispositional stress reactivity. Distinct discriminant-validity analyses found no rs53576 association with attachment anxiety or avoidance (F(1,104)=1.20 and1.02; avoidance P=.315), or parental care. Anxiety P is not printed in that paragraph and is not reconstructed.
access_limits: Endpoint-specific complete-case Ns differ; enrollment192 is not attachment-analysis N.
No raw-data/sample-overlap linkage to Gillath/Pearce established.

originals.citation: Smith, Travis R., Kelsey Panfil, and Kimberly Kirkpatrick (2022). Generalizability of time-based interventions: Effects of choice procedure and smaller-sooner delay. Behavioural Processes 196, 104584.
originals.first_page_check: Complete NIH accepted-manuscript front identifies exact title/three authors/DOI and final publication196:104584. Article number, not conventional first-page number; publisher typeset PDF not recovered.
originals.design_and_sample: Independent incoming cohorts36/48 male Sprague-Dawley rats,84total; arrived separately. Experiment1:18 delayed-FI vs18 no-delay;45sessions,15SS/30LL; FI5s one pellet/FI30s two pellets versus immediate FI0 (functionally FR2), with ITIs65/90s matching FI interreinforcer intervals. Subsequent SYS/ADJ choice order counterbalanced; first-choice data analyzed because of order effects; final SYS SS-delay assessment.
originals.published_finding: Experiment1 ADJ point-of-subjective-equality15.5s FI versus15.9s ND, no significant group effect. SYS unexpectedly showed fewer LL choices after delayed FI than ND (at middle LL30s z=-2.42,P=.016; middle SS20s z=-2.33,P=.020). Experiment2 used pre/post choice and delayed-FI5/10s combinations, NO ND or handled control; incongruent delays worsened self-control, congruent10/10 improved intermediate-delay LL choice.
access_limits: NIH accepted manuscript, not verified against typeset publisher proof.
No original raw dataset or supplement analyses downloaded; body explicitly states Experiment1 conference presentations in2019.
No experiment directly estimates immediate exposure versus a handled/no-experience maturation control within Smith2022.

A.current_comparison: Study2 randomly endowed prospective three-fact bundle versus no endowment; all chose three versus four unrevealed trivia facts. This is the information-ownership preference corresponding conceptually to WTA/WTP asymmetry, with no monetary bidding or instrumental sales use. It does not remeasure a numerical WTA/WTP ratio or source-copy/expertise interaction. Actual retention comparison68%vs46%,N146.
A.confounds: Current authors distinguish (1) BDM/risk-aversion interpretation; (2) paying money versus receiving money introducing a money-loss asymmetry; (3) possible instrumental game-profit value. Original2003 itself also discusses strategically high BDM bids to secure information at unknown market prices. These are substantive elicitation distinctions, not proof that no prior finding is revisited.
A.report_chain: JAIS2003 N31 (29retained); conference2003 N55 (groups31/24,135 retained paired bid observations from141); conference explicitly refers to JAIS-title paper under review for experimental-session details. This establishes an explicit companion-report link but not participant-level overlap. 2006 author abstract N294 adds source-nature/status factors. Changed author order/year cannot settle whether2006 extends/reuses any earlier data; no equivalence or independence asserted.
A.shipped_relation: Actual shipped row801 is Tversky/Kahneman1981 DOI10.1126/science.7455683. Current Methods explicitly models Study3 Asian Disease framing; it is separate from Study2 information endowment.

B.current_comparison: Current2018 study uses same analyses as Pearce2017 on two independent participant subsets collected contemporaneously: white prior-mental-illness group140 and nonwhite/no-illness group66. Previously published healthy-white data are reused as comparator, not a wholly fresh healthy-white replication sample.
B.measure_relationship: All three papers address OXTR rs53576 and anxious/avoidant attachment dimensions. Current12-item seven-point short-form ECR explicitly asks about close friendships. Gillath uses36-item standard ECR; Rodrigues uses shortened romantic ECR with five-point response. Thus there is a genotype/attachment-domain relationship plus material relationship-target/measurement differences. Rodrigues positive empathy/stress endpoints are distinct from its attachment nulls.
B.group_specific_findings: Current Results report rs53576 lower anxiety with more minor alleles in subclinical sample; that is NOT a null. Discussion null comparison appears immediately after rs237897 association in the two no-illness samples. It cannot be generalized to the subclinical sample or to all OXTR endpoints. Complete SNP-by-group null/testability details require current supplementary tables; no absent body association automatically counted as a tested null.
B.closest_published_chain: The current authors explicitly anchor same-analysis comparison to shipped Pearce2017 (row2469 DOI10.1073/pnas.1700712114), and identify rs237897/anxiety in healthy-white and nonwhite no-illness groups as a specific shared SNP finding. They separately explicitly compare rs53576 attachment nulls to Gillath2008 and Rodrigues2009. These are different SNP findings. Pearce2017 is closest declared operational comparison, but this alone does not prove it exhausts every specific rs53576 null comparison.
remaining_limits: No independently recovered Pearce2017 original body within this five-original task; its exact rs53576 attachment tables and ancestral citation chain remain independently unverified.
Current supplementary tables not upgraded; precise nonsignificant models versus untestable models by sample remain unresolved where not explicitly stated in current body.
No claim that posthoc/Discussion placement excludes a finding relationship; no final target judgment.

C.current_comparison: Fox2024 uses48 male Wistar rats, two24-rat cohorts,randomized within cohort to24ND/24handled-maturation;47days FR2 immediate reinforcement with1/2pellets,mean6629.54trials,then posttest-only RIFI choice:SSR5s/1pellet versusLLR10/20/30s/2pellets.
C.actual_smith_contrast: Smith2022 has genuine FR2-equivalent immediate-exposure ND training in Experiment1, but directly compares it with delayed FI, not untreated maturation. Its SYS result favors ND over delayed-FI at middle delays, while the ND choice slope is steeper and both groups floor at60s. Experiment2 compares delayed5/10s training/choice combinations and has noND. This is a substantially more specific relationship than generic immediate training increases impulsivity.
C.finding_chain: Fox2024 names Smith2022 with Fox2022,Fox2019,Renda2018 both before Methods and at the opening Discussion comparison. Smith’s own Discussion specifically links increased delay sensitivity after ND/short-delay exposure to Fox(2021), identified in its reference list by title and DOI10.1002/jeab.727, the same DOI current Fox2024 dates2022. Smith also lists Fox etal2019, but that entry alone is not the cited support for this particular Discussion sentence. Fox2024’s doubled sample/trials sentence specifically names Fox2022/Fox2019; it is not a doubling claim about Smith’s36/48 cohorts.
C.shipped_relation: Actual shipped1480 is Renda etal2018 DOI10.1002/jeab.432. Smith2022 is a distinct authored report with identified independent Experiment1/2 cohorts. No evidence makes it the same report/data as shipped Renda2018. Existing positive Fox originals were not recoded or edited.
remaining_limits: Whether Fox’s generalization invokes a separately remeasured Smith-specific finding versus comparing a partly ancestral timing literature remains a parent adjudication question.
Source supports a real immediate-exposure condition; neither parenthetical citation nor procedural changes alone establishes an exclusion. No final target/outcome label.

A_current_closest.quote: The current research is closest to a set of studies in information science conducted by Rafaeli and Raban (27, 28), who replicated the endowment effect for information in a game mimicking sales decisions.

A_current_confound.quote: Second, their observed preferences over information may be confounded by attitudes toward gaining and losing money, since their willingness-to-pay measure involved giving up money (which, due to loss aversion, people are reluctant to do), while their willingness-to-accept measure involved obtaining money.

A_current_instrumentality.quote: If that information was perceived to directly translate into financial rewards, it is impossible to determine whether the observed effect reflected loss aversion for information per se or for the in-game profits.

A_current_design.quote: We recruited 146 adult participants from Prolific (45% female, 54% male, 1% other; age: Range: 18-74, Median = 29, M = 33.0, SD = 12.6) and randomly assigned them to one of two conditions: endowed or nonendowed.

A_current_effect.quote: Indeed, participants in the endowed condition were more likely to prefer learning just three facts (68%) than those in the nonendowed condition (46%) (χ2(1, n = 146) = 7.03, P = 0.008, Φ = 0.219) (Fig. 2).

A_current_asian.quote: We modeled our experiment on the classic “Asian Disease” problem, which Tversky and Kahneman (21) [see also (22)] originally used to demonstrate the gain-loss framing effect.

B_current_null_statement.quote: Although we replicate previous null findings for attachment style and one of the most widely studied SNPs, OXTR rs53576 (Gillath et al. 2008 ; Rodrigues et al. 2009 ), this corroborative result for rs237897 illustrates the importance of parallel testing of a number of different SNPs for each gene, rather than focusing on a few popular ones.

B_current_measure.quote: Dispositional attachment styles (avoidant and anxious dimensions) in close friendships (rather than romantic/sexual relationships) were measured using the short-form Experiences of Close Relationships scale (Wei et al. 2007 ).

B_current_group_effect.quote: For example, Anxious Attachment was linked to OXTR variation in all three samples: rs237897 ( geno_2df effect) in the healthy Caucasian and non-white samples (as discussed above) and both the rs53576 (the more minor alleles carried the lower the anxiety) and rs2228485 ( geno_2df effect) in the subclinical sample.

B_current_chain.quote: To build on these previous findings, we conducted the same analyses on two smaller independent samples from genetically and clinically distinct populations, the data for which were collected at the same time as those reported in Pearce et al. ( 2017 ).

B_current_r237897.quote: Thirdly, the OXTR SNP rs237897 was significantly associated with Anxious Attachment in both Caucasians and non-Caucasians who did not report a history of mental illness (Pearce et al. 2017 ).

C_current_discussion_chain.quote:
A group of rats was exposed to an immediate (no-delay)-

reinforcement intervention and subsequent delay discounting

behavior was modestly, but statistically signiﬁcantly, more

impulsive compared to a control group. This is consistent

with previous work (Fox, 2022; Fox etal., 2019; Renda

etal., 2018; Smith etal., 2022), and with the conclusion
that prolonged exposure to immediate reinforcement may

have just modest impacts on subsequent impulsive choice,

compared to relatively larger impacts of exposure to delayed

reinforcement. This was true in the present experiment

despite double the number of subjects in each group and

double the number of immediate reinforcement training tri-

als, compared to previous research (Fox 2022; Fox etal.,

2019). This indicates that perhaps more training does not
necessarily translate to larger shifts in choice behavior, con-

sistent with work investigating training parameters during

a delay exposure paradigm designed to reduce impulsive

choice (Renda etal., 2020).
